name: SearchImage
title: Search by Image
description: Find the web pages a picture appears on, via SearchAPI.io (Google Lens)
whenToUse: Pick when you HAVE A PICTURE and want the pages it appears on: the same photo reused on a speaker page, an event listing, an article or a profile (Google Lens). It takes an image link, not words, and returns the pages that show it, exact copies first, then pages with pictures that look alike. Finding pages or images from a keyword query is a different job.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Upstream data; the image link usually templates from it

outputs.name: matches
outputs.description: The pages the picture appears on (title, url, source, thumbnail, exact). Exact copies of the picture come first with exact true, then pages with pictures that look alike.

outputs.name: note
outputs.description: Why there are no matches, in the vendor's words, when it said: the picture could not be loaded (try another), or no results. Empty when the search found pages.

imageUrl.title: Image URL
imageUrl.description: A public link to the picture to search with. The vendor fetches it, so it must load without signing in.

numResults.title: Number of Results
numResults.description: Most pages to return, exact copies counted first

country.title: Country
country.description: Country code for localized results, e.g. 'us', 'uk', 'ae'

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: search
package.packageFile:
# FULLY DECLARATIVE. Five nodes, one endpoint, one key.
#
# SearchAPI.io is the cleanest case for this format: every engine is the SAME url switched
# by `engine=`, authenticated by one `api_key` in the query. `shared/searchapi.yaml` holds
# the call, each node names its engine and shapes its own reply, and the whole client is
# gone: `auth: apiKeyQuery` was already an executor capability.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/search/`.

name: search
displayName: Search
description: Web, news, video, places and by-image search via SearchAPI.io
version: 2.0.0
category: search
logoUrl: https://cdn-icons-png.flaticon.com/512/3128/3128287.png

features:
  - Google web and image results
  - Google News, dated articles
  - YouTube video search
  - Google Maps places with ratings
  - Google Lens, the pages a picture appears on

allowedHosts:
  - www.searchapi.io

requires:
  credential: [apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  executorVersion: ">=1.0.0"

credentials.searchapiCredential.yaml:
# One key powers every engine in this package. Transcribed from src/credentials/index.ts.

name: searchapiCredential
displayName: SearchAPI
description: SearchAPI.io credentials. One key powers every search engine in this package.
documentationUrl: https://www.searchapi.io/docs

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your SearchAPI.io API key
    placeholder: ""

shared.searchapi.yaml:
# The ONE call every node in this package makes.
#
# Same url, same auth, switched by `engine`. A node $refs this and layers its own `query`
# keys on top, which is what a $ref with siblings does: imported first, local wins.
#
# The key travels as a query parameter because that is what the vendor takes. `apiKeyQuery`
# is an executor capability, so no node handles a secret itself.

call: &call
  method: GET
  url: https://www.searchapi.io/api/v1/search
  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyQuery
    param: api_key
    value: "{{ credentials.searchapiCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

# A 200 is not always a success here: the vendor reports a bad parameter or an exhausted
# quota in the body. Without this a failed search emits empty results and reads as "nothing
# found", which is the wrong answer rather than an error.
#
# Except "nothing found" itself: the vendor reports an empty search in the same field
# ("Google didn't return any results."). That IS the answer, so it emits empty lists, and a
# search for a person with no news does not end the run.
error: &error
  when: "return !!response.error && !String(response.error).includes(\"didn't return any results\")"
  message: "return typeof response.error === 'string' ? response.error : JSON.stringify(response.error)"

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# EXACT COPIES FIRST. A page showing the very same picture is far stronger evidence than one
# showing a picture that looks like it, so the two lists are kept apart by `exact` rather than
# merged into one undifferentiated ranking. A `data:` thumbnail is dropped, as in SearchWeb.
# Reads `calls.lens`, because a skipped search leaves no key and the list is then empty.

- emit: matches
  from: response
  value: >-
    return [].concat(
      ((calls.lens || {}).exact_matches || []).map(m => ({ m: m, exact: true })),
      ((calls.lens || {}).visual_matches || []).map(m => ({ m: m, exact: false }))
    ).slice(0, config.numResults || 20).map(x => ({
      title: x.m.title || "",
      url: x.m.link || "",
      source: x.m.source || "",
      thumbnail: (x.m.thumbnail || "").startsWith("data:") ? "" : x.m.thumbnail || "",
      exact: x.exact
    }))

- emit: note
  from: response
  # Why there are no matches when the vendor said why: "could not load the image" (try another
  # picture) or "didn't return any results". Empty when the search ran and found pages.
  value: "return String((calls.lens || {}).error || '')"
files.api/run.yaml:
# One call. `all` returns both lists, exact copies and look-alikes, in one reply.
#
# NO PICTURE, NO CALL: an empty link skips the search and the node answers no matches,
# rather than failing the run it sits in (the vendor refuses a search with no url).
#
# A PICTURE LENS CANNOT LOAD IS AN ANSWER, not a failure: an expired or mistyped link, or a host
# that refuses Google, comes back as a 400 "could not load the image". The caller tries another
# picture, so the node answers no matches and says why in `note`, and the run goes on.

- $ref: searchapi#call
  name: lens
  when: "return String(config.imageUrl || '').trim().length > 0"
  okOn: [400]
  error:
    when: >-
      return !!response.error && !String(response.error).includes("didn't return any results")
        && !String(response.error).includes("could not load the image")
    message: "return typeof response.error === 'string' ? response.error : JSON.stringify(response.error)"
  query:
    engine: google_lens
    url: "{{ config.imageUrl }}"
    search_type: all
    country: "return String(config.country || 'us').toUpperCase()"
    hl: "{{ config.language }}"
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [imageUrl]
  properties:
    imageUrl:
      type: string
      title: Image URL
      description: A public link to the picture to search with. The vendor fetches it, so it must load without signing in.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    numResults:
      type: number
      title: Number of Results
      description: Most pages to return, exact copies counted first
      default: 20
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100
    country:
      type: string
      title: Country
      description: Country code for localized results, e.g. 'us', 'uk', 'ae'
      default: us
    language:
      type: string
      title: Language
      description: Language code for results, e.g. 'en', 'ar'
      default: en
"ui:order": [imageUrl, numResults, country, language]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Upstream data; the image link usually templates from it
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: matches
    type: array
    description: >-
      The pages the picture appears on (title, url, source, thumbnail, exact). Exact copies of
      the picture come first with exact true, then pages with pictures that look alike.
  - name: note
    type: string
    description: >-
      Why there are no matches, in the vendor's words, when it said: the picture could not be
      loaded (try another), or no results. Empty when the search found pages.

credentials:
  - name: searchapiCredential
    required: true
    displayName: SearchAPI
files.node.yaml:
type: SearchImage
kind: PromiseNode
name: Search by Image
category: Search
color: "#4285F4"
description: Find the web pages a picture appears on, via SearchAPI.io (Google Lens)
whenToUse: >
  Pick when you HAVE A PICTURE and want the pages it appears on: the same photo reused on a
  speaker page, an event listing, an article or a profile (Google Lens). It takes an image
  link, not words, and returns the pages that show it, exact copies first, then pages with
  pictures that look alike. Finding pages or images from a keyword query is a different job.

auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Idempotent read: the same picture yields the same pages.
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
testData:
  config:
    imageUrl: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a9/Example.jpg
    numResults: 10
    country: us
    language: en
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    matches: "return output.matches.length > 0 && typeof output.matches[0].url === 'string'"
